answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. The result is a self-purifying economy: every epoch, low-cost fake identities are filtered out by the same reputation mechanics that reward the honest ones. Consider a gale as the anchor of the cost.
